messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — ACME reporting 500s from /v1/rerank. They say it started after a pipeline change that inserted null bytes and some complex emoji sequences (ZWJ clusters). @kevin_eng can you take a look?

customer_acme: Repro summary: ~3% of our batch rerank calls return 500. Payload includes candidate text with both \u0000 bytes (from legacy ETL) and emoji like 👩‍👩‍👧‍👦 or family sequences. Attached minimal curl below.

customer_acme: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"query":"Find family photos","candidates":["normal candidate","hello\u0000world 👨‍👩‍👧","👩\u200d👩\u200d👧\u200d👦 name"]}'
```

maria_support: They included the full response: 500 + body: {"error":"internal_server_error","message":"utf8 decode error: invalid continuation byte at pos 18"} X-Request-ID: rq_abc123

kevin_eng: Thanks. Trying to repro now. Can you confirm whether the null byte is literally \u0000 in JSON or actual 0x00 bytes in the UTF-8 payload? Also which SDK (node/python) they used.

customer_acme: It's from a Python ETL that writes UTF-8 to a message queue; we saw \u0000 show up after a bad legacy transform, so the HTTP body contains real 0x00 bytes when the SDK serializes. Using our Node service to call rerank (node-fetch).

kevin_eng: Reproduced locally by crafting a request with an embedded 0x00 and an emoji ZWJ sequence split across a boundary. Getting 500 and runtime log: "tokenizer: invalid surrogate half (0xD83D) at byte 22". Looks like our pre-tokenizer assumes well-formed UTF-8 and chokes when surrogate pairs are split by inserted NULs.

kevin_eng: Minimal repro (node):
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const body = {
  query: 'x',
  candidates: ['normal','hi\u0000\ud83d\ude00'] // null then emoji half
};
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank',{method:'POST',headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer sk-...','Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify(body)})
.then(r=>r.text()).then(t=>console.log('resp',t));
```

jess_sre: Pulled the runtime logs for pool=rerank-pool-usw2. Saw repeated panics in the tokenization stage when encountering 0x00 between UTF-8 code points. Stack points to kv-cache transform -> tokenizer.c: validate_utf8().

jess_sre: Short-term mitigation: recommend client-side sanitization to drop or replace NULs and to normalize combining sequences (NFC). `candidate = candidate.replace(/\u0000/g, '')` or `normalize('NFC')`.

kevin_eng: Filed INF-789: "rerank: robust UTF-8 handling for NULs and broken surrogate sequences". Plan: add byte-level UTF-8 validation early in request pipeline, convert invalid subsequences to U+FFFD or return 400 with clear diagnostics. Also add unit tests for ZWJ and surrogate-split cases.

runtime-bot: Deploy started: release/utf8-guard v1.2.1 -> canary (rerank-pool-usw2). CI tests include new malformed-utf8 cases.

kevin_eng: Patch note: we now sanitize candidate texts before tokenization, replacing lone NULs and merging broken surrogate halves into replacement char. We also surface a `400` with `malformed_input` when a payload cannot be safely normalized. This prevents 500s.

customer_acme: Thanks — we'll add sanitizer on our side for now and monitor. Please ping when canary is healthy.

jess_sre: Canary healthy after 15m, no regressions. Rolling to remaining pools. INF-789 will also include a guidance doc for SDKs.

maria_support: Marking as escalated -> resolved. Follow-up action: add SDK snippets for client-side sanitizers and update support KB. :thumbsup:
